embeds.title: 🟡 Mini Shai-Hulud Worm Compromises npm and PyPI Packages from TanStack, UiPath, Mistral AI, OpenSearch, and Guardrails AI
embeds.description:
**Actor:** TeamPCP
TeamPCP has been linked to a supply chain attack campaign called Mini Shai-Hulud that compromised npm and PyPI packages from TanStack, UiPath, Mistral AI, OpenSearch, and Guardrails AI. The malware injects obfuscated JavaScript to steal credentials targeting cloud providers, cryptocurrency wallets, AI tools, and CI systems, exfiltrating data to attacker-controlled infrastructure. TanStack confirmed the compromise involved a chained GitHub Actions attack using pull_request_target triggers and OIDC token extraction. The worm spreads by locating publishable npm tokens and exchanging GitHub OIDC tokens for per-package publish tokens. The TanStack compromise has been assigned CVE-2026-45321 with a CVSS score of 9.6, impacting 42 packages and 84 versions. The campaign has also spread to PyPI packages including guardrails-ai, mistralai, and opensearch-project packages, with the mistralai package containing geofenced destructive logic and the guardrails-ai package executing malicious code on import.
**Sources:** thehackernews.com • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-45321 • **Access:** Supply chain compromise via GitHub Actions pull_request_target trigger and cache poisoning
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** reported
